title: Dual-variable force characterisation method for human–robot interaction in wearable robotics
authors: Felipe Ballen-Moreno | Pasquale Ferrentino | Milan Amighi | Bram Vanderborght | Tom Verstraten
finding: Panda end-effector with a Medusa six-axis force/torque sensor presses and twists at four forearm phantom sites. Section 2.5 interpolates measured curves to compare candidate material fits. This supplies force/torque responses against commanded protocol and robot displacement/rotation, without an independently logged bias reference or contact-free force truth.

title: Modeling and design of geared DC motors for energy efficiency: Comparison between theory and experiments
authors: T. Verstraten | G. Mathijssen | R. Furnémont | B. Vanderborght | D. Lefeber
locator: §5 experimental validation, test setup and Fig. 10; §§5.6.1–5.6.2
finding: Position-controlled geared pendulum uses an output-side shaft transducer, motor-terminal current/voltage, and shaft encoders. The EPOS2 current and position loops run at 10 kHz and 1 kHz. Converter losses are invisible to motor-terminal measurements. Separate damping losses across components require additional instrumentation.

title: Series and Parallel Elastic Actuation: Impact of natural dynamics on power and energy consumption
authors: Tom Verstraten | Philipp Beckerle | Raphaël Furnémont | Glenn Mathijssen | Bram Vanderborght | Dirk Lefeber
locator: §4.1 and Fig. 6; §4 experimental data and Table 3; ref. [32]
finding: Flexible and rigid drive configurations share an instrumented pendulum. Gearbox shaft torque (20 Nm DRBK transducer) and encoder determine mechanical energy; the load-shaft encoder and electrical current/voltage readings distinguish motion and electrical consumption. Supports placement of references, with no open time-series file verified.

title: Series and Parallel Elastic Actuation: Influence of Operating Positions on Design and Control
authors: Philipp Beckerle | Tom Verstraten | Glenn Mathijssen | Raphael Furnemont | Bram Vanderborght | Dirk Lefeber
locator: Experimental investigation, Fig. 5 and Figs. 6–7; refs. [19], [21]
finding: Gearbox shaft transducer and optical encoder measure mechanical power; the supply current and voltage give electrical consumption. Separate load-side angle and gearbox-side position during cyclic motion reveal how rest-angle offsets shift energy optima. These mechanical equilibrium offsets do not label sensor drift.

title: An energy efficiency index for elastic actuators during resonant motion
locator: Table 4; experimental validation and Fig. 9; references [4] and [49]
finding: A series elastic bench records two optical encoder positions across 4 load inertias × 6 oscillation amplitudes. At lowest inertia the analytical index omitting temporary energy overpredicts efficiency. Stiction, misalignment and cogging can affect the measured index. This is a model-validation counterexample, without measured post-limiter commands.

title: +SPEA introduction: Drastic actuator energy requirement reduction by symbiosis of parallel motors, springs and locking mechanisms
authors: Glenn Mathijssen | Raphael Furnemont | Tom Verstraten | Branko Brackx | Jasmina Premec | Rene Jimenez | Dirk Lefeber | Bram Vanderborght
locator: §III.C Test set-up, Fig. 2 and experimental comparison of brake configurations
finding: Four drive units supply current/velocity readouts; the output link connects to the frame through a DRBK-200 transducer, which independently measures net output torque. Motor voltage is inferred via a model and brake consumption omitted from that model. Distinguishes direct reaction from model-derived quantities.
